entries.head: hang out

senses.zh: 没具体安排地一起待着
senses.en: to spend time with people without a specific plan

example.en: We just hung out at my place and watched old movies.
example.zh: 我们就在我家待着看了几部老电影。

entries.l1_note: “一起玩”不是 play together（那是小孩）；成年人是 hang out。

entries.head: catch up

senses.en: to meet someone and talk about what has happened

example.en: Let's catch up over coffee next week.
example.zh: 下周找时间喝咖啡聊聊近况。

senses.en: to reach someone who is ahead of you

example.en: Run ahead — I'll catch up at the corner.
example.zh: 你先跑，我在路口追上你。

entries.l1_note: “叙旧”不是 talk old things；catch up 才是那个词。

entries.head: get along

senses.en: to have a good relationship with someone

example.en: My roommate and I get along better than I expected.
example.zh: 我和室友处得比想象中好。

entries.l1_note: 合得来是 get along (with)，不是 get well with。

entries.head: tag along

senses.en: to go with someone, often without being invited

example.en: Mind if I tag along? I don't know anyone there.
example.zh: 我跟着去可以吗？那边我一个人都不认识。

entries.l1_note: “跟着去”不是 go with them；tag along 带“不请自来、蹭着去”的味道。

entries.head: join in

senses.en: to take part in an activity that is already happening

example.en: Everyone was singing, so I joined in.
example.zh: 大家都在唱，我也跟着唱了。

entries.l1_note: join 是加入组织，join in 是加入正在进行的活动；中文都叫“加入”。

entries.head: warm up to

senses.zh: 一开始不喜欢，后来接受
senses.en: to start to like someone or something gradually

example.en: I didn't like him at first, but I'm warming up to him.
example.zh: 我一开始不喜欢他，但现在慢慢接受了。

entries.l1_note: “慢慢接受”不是 accept slowly 才自然；warm up to 指态度转暖。

entries.head: strike up

senses.en: to start a conversation or friendship

example.en: He struck up a conversation with the person next to him.
example.zh: 他跟旁边的人聊了起来。

entries.l1_note: 攀谈是 strike up a conversation，不是 start a talk（中式）。

entries.head: hit it off

senses.en: to like each other immediately

example.en: We hit it off right away and talked for two hours.
example.zh: 我们一见如故，聊了两个小时。

entries.l1_note: 一见如故是 hit it off，不是 get along at once（生硬）。

entries.head: go on about

senses.en: to keep talking about something

example.en: He keeps going on about his new phone.
example.zh: 他一直在讲他的新手机。

entries.l1_note: go on about 带不耐烦的意味，不是普通“说”。

entries.head: drone on

senses.en: to talk for a long time in a boring voice

example.en: The speaker droned on for an hour.
example.zh: 演讲者干巴巴讲了一小时。

entries.l1_note: drone on 带贬义，指声音单调。

entries.head: ramble on

senses.en: to talk without a clear point

example.en: Sorry for rambling on — I'm just nervous.
example.zh: 抱歉扯远了，我就是紧张。

entries.l1_note: ramble on 是没重点地讲，不是散步（ramble）。

entries.head: cut in

senses.en: to interrupt someone who is speaking

example.en: Sorry to cut in, but the taxi's here.
example.zh: 不好意思打断一下，车到了。

entries.l1_note: 插话是 cut in；插队（车）也是 cut in，看语境。

entries.head: jump in

senses.en: to start taking part in a conversation

example.en: Feel free to jump in if I miss anything.
example.zh: 我漏了什么你随时插话。

entries.l1_note: jump in 是主动加入，语气比 cut in 友好。

entries.head: chime in

senses.en: to add a comment to a conversation

example.en: Several people chimed in with the same idea.
example.zh: 好几个人附和了同一个想法。

entries.l1_note: chime in 是友好地补充，不是敲钟（chime）。

entries.head: butt in

senses.en: to interrupt rudely

example.en: Don't butt in when adults are talking.

entries.l1_note: butt in 比 cut in 更粗鲁，带责备。

entries.head: get through to

senses.en: to make someone understand what you mean

example.en: I just can't get through to my dad about this.
example.zh: 这事我就是跟我爸说不通。

entries.l1_note: get through to 有两个意思：让人听进去、电话打通。

entries.head: put across

senses.en: to explain an idea clearly

example.en: She put her point across without sounding aggressive.
example.zh: 她把观点讲清楚了，又不显得咄咄逼人。

entries.l1_note: put across 是表达清楚；put on 是穿、假装。

entries.head: get across

senses.en: to succeed in making people understand

example.en: The diagram helped get the idea across.

entries.l1_note: get across 强调“成功传达”，put across 强调“去表达”。

entries.head: talk over

senses.en: to discuss something thoroughly

example.en: Let's talk it over before we tell the team.

entries.l1_note: talk over 是商量；talk over someone 是盖过别人说话。

entries.head: talk through

senses.en: to explain or discuss step by step

example.en: Can you talk me through what happened?
example.zh: 你能一步步说说发生了什么吗？

entries.l1_note: talk through 是过一遍流程；talk over 是商量。

entries.head: hear out

senses.en: to listen to someone until they finish

example.en: Hear me out before you say no.

entries.l1_note: 听人说完是 hear someone out，代词夹中间。

entries.head: tune out

senses.en: to stop paying attention

example.en: I tuned out halfway through the lecture.
example.zh: 讲座听到一半我就走神了。

entries.l1_note: tune out 是主动不听；tune in 是收听。

entries.head: zone out

senses.en: to stop thinking about what is happening

example.en: Sorry, I zoned out — what did you say?
example.zh: 抱歉我走神了，你说什么？

entries.l1_note: zone out 是发呆；不是“进区”（zone）。

entries.head: space out

senses.en: to become inattentive for a moment

example.en: He spaced out and missed his stop.

entries.l1_note: space out 和 zone out 近似，美式都很常用。

entries.head: nod along

senses.en: to nod while someone talks, sometimes without understanding

example.en: I just nodded along and hoped nobody asked me anything.
example.zh: 我就跟着点头，祈祷没人问我。

entries.l1_note: nod along 常暗示“其实没听懂”，带自嘲。

entries.head: laugh off

senses.en: to treat something as a joke to avoid dealing with it

example.en: He laughed off the mistake, but everyone noticed.
example.zh: 他一笑带过，但大家都看见了。

entries.l1_note: 一笑置之是 laugh off，不是 laugh away。

entries.head: open up

senses.en: to start talking honestly about feelings

example.en: It took a few drinks before he opened up.
example.zh: 喝了几杯他才开始说心里话。

entries.l1_note: 敞开心扉是 open up；open 单独是打开东西。

entries.head: loosen up

senses.en: to become more relaxed

example.en: Loosen up — nobody here is judging you.
example.zh: 放松点，这儿没人评判你。

entries.l1_note: loosen up 是劝人别紧张，不是把衣服弄松。

entries.head: lighten up

senses.en: to stop being so serious

example.en: Lighten up — it's just a game.
example.zh: 别那么严肃，就是个游戏。

entries.l1_note: lighten up 是让人别较真，语气轻松；对上级少用。

entries.head: come over

senses.en: to come to someone's home or place

example.en: Come over for hot pot this weekend.
example.zh: 这周末来我家吃火锅吧。

entries.l1_note: 过来是 come over；come to my home 太生硬。

entries.head: take part in

senses.en: to be involved in an activity

example.en: She took part in the company's charity run.
example.zh: 她参加了公司的慈善跑。

entries.l1_note: take part in + 活动；participate in 更正式。

entries.head: in one's element

senses.en: to be comfortable doing something you are good at

example.en: She's in her element when she's hosting a party.
example.zh: 她办派对的时候如鱼得水。

entries.l1_note: in one's element 是“如鱼得水”；out of one's element 是不自在。

entries.head: associate with

senses.en: 与……来往

example.en: I don't associate with people who gossip at work.
example.zh: 我不跟上班爱八卦的人来往。

entries.l1_note: associate with + 人；be associated with 是“与…有关”。

entries.head: come from

senses.en: 来自；出身

example.en: She comes from a small city in Sichuan.
example.zh: 她来自四川的一个小城市。

entries.l1_note: come from + 地方；不是“从……来”只能用进行时。

entries.head: remind of

senses.en: 使想起

example.en: This song reminds me of my college days.
example.zh: 这首歌让我想起大学时光。

entries.l1_note: remind someone of something；不是“提醒某人做”。

entries.head: clown around

senses.en: 胡闹

example.en: Stop clowning around and help me.

entries.l1_note: clown around 是胡闹；不是“小丑”。

entries.head: joke around

senses.en: 开玩笑

example.en: We were just joking around — don't take it seriously.
example.zh: 我们只是开玩笑，别当真。

entries.l1_note: joke around 是不及物；不是“取笑某人”。

entries.head: kid around

senses.en: 逗着玩

example.en: I was just kidding around about your haircut.
example.zh: 我拿你发型开玩笑而已。

entries.l1_note: kid around 是逗着玩；不是“小孩”。

entries.head: listen in

senses.en: 偷听

example.en: Someone was listening in on our call.
example.zh: 有人在偷听我们的电话。

entries.l1_note: listen in on + 对话；不是“听进去”。

entries.head: listen up

senses.en: 注意听

example.en: Listen up — there's been a change of plan.

entries.l1_note: listen up 是口语“注意听”；不礼貌程度低于 shut up。

example.en: I read in my free time.
I'm into photography these days.
I collect tickets from every trip.
example.zh: 每次旅行的票我都收集。

example.en: We go for a walk after dinner.
He plays the guitar on weekends.
Photography is a hobby of mine.
I took up running last year.
She joined a book club.
I enjoy cooking on weekends.
Try something new this month.
I stick to the same breakfast every day.
example.zh: 我每天坚持同样的早饭。

example.en: As a rule, I don't work on Sundays.
I used to run every morning.
We meet on a regular basis.
Most of the time I cook at home.
example.zh: 大多数时候我在家做饭。

example.en: We eat out from time to time.
I swim once a week.
He works at the store day in, day out.
example.zh: 他日复一日在店里上班。

example.en: I check my phone out of habit.

entries.head: get into the habit of doing something

example.en: I got into the habit of walking to work.
example.zh: 我养成了走路上班的习惯。

example.en: The new place is good; let's go again.

variants.head: great

example.en: The food was great.

variants.note_zh: 比 good 更热情，口语最常用。

variants.head: solid

example.en: It's a solid choice.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调可靠、不错；不是“坚固”。

variants.head: awesome

example.en: That's awesome news; congratulations!

variants.note_zh: 比 great 更兴奋，偏年轻；口语常用。

example.en: The movie was bad, but the popcorn was good.
example.zh: 电影不怎么样，爆米花倒不错。

variants.head: terrible

example.en: The traffic was terrible.

variants.note_zh: 比 bad 重，明确否定；正式和口语都能用。

variants.head: awful

example.en: The food was awful.

variants.note_zh: 比 bad 重，口语常用；带明显嫌弃。

variants.head: rough

example.en: It was a rough week.

variants.note_zh: 口语，指日子不好过/状态差；不是“粗糙”。

example.en: She's smart and quick to learn.

variants.head: clever

example.en: That's a clever solution.

variants.note_zh: 偏点子巧妙；比 smart 更强调“机灵”。

variants.head: sharp

example.en: She's sharp; she catches everything.
example.zh: 她脑子快，什么都听得出。

variants.note_zh: 口语，反应快、观察敏锐。

variants.head: brilliant

example.en: He's brilliant at math.

variants.note_zh: 程度重；英式口语里也常表示“很棒”。

example.en: I'm lazy on weekends and stay in bed.

variants.head: laid-back

example.en: He's laid-back about deadlines.

variants.note_zh: 中性偏褒，指不紧张；不是“懒”。

variants.head: slacking

example.en: Stop slacking and finish the report.

variants.note_zh: 口语，正在偷懒；比 lazy 更具体。

variants.head: idle

example.en: The machines sat idle all day.

variants.note_zh: 偏书面，指闲置/不运转；也可说人无所事事。

example.en: The street is noisy at night.

variants.head: loud

example.en: The music is too loud.

variants.note_zh: 最常用，指音量大；比 noisy 更直接。

variants.head: deafening

example.en: The music was deafening.

variants.note_zh: 程度重，偏书面；强调吵到受不了。

variants.head: rowdy

example.en: The bar got rowdy after ten.

variants.note_zh: 多指一群人喧闹；不是单纯音量大。

example.en: The library is quiet in the morning.

variants.head: silent

example.en: The room went silent.

variants.note_zh: 比 quiet 更绝对，一点声音都没有。

variants.head: hushed

example.en: They spoke in hushed voices.

variants.note_zh: 偏书面，指刻意压低声音；不是环境安静。

variants.head: peaceful

example.en: The park is peaceful in the morning.

variants.note_zh: 褒义，强调让人放松；不是“没声音”。

example.en: He's funny without even trying.

variants.head: hilarious

example.en: The show was hilarious.

variants.note_zh: 比 funny 重，笑到不行；口语常用。

variants.head: amusing

example.en: It was an amusing story.
example.zh: 那是个挺有意思的故事。

variants.note_zh: 轻微笑意，比 funny 正式；不是大笑。

variants.head: a riot

example.en: He's a riot at parties.

variants.note_zh: 口语，形容人特别搞笑；不是“暴乱”。

example.en: I'm serious about learning English.

variants.head: no joke

example.en: The deadline is no joke.
example.zh: 这个截止日期不是开玩笑的。

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调事情严重；不是“没笑话”。

variants.head: dead serious

example.en: I'm dead serious about quitting.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调态度认真；比 serious 重。

variants.head: in earnest

example.en: They started planning in earnest.

variants.note_zh: 偏书面，指正式开始认真做；日常口语少用。

example.en: She's kind to everyone she meets.
example.zh: 她对遇到的人都很善良。

variants.head: thoughtful

example.en: That was a thoughtful gift.

variants.note_zh: 强调替别人着想；比 kind 更具体。

variants.head: considerate

example.en: She's considerate of her neighbors.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，强调顾及他人感受。

variants.head: sweet

example.en: That's so sweet of you.

variants.note_zh: 口语，偏感情上的好；不是“甜”。

example.en: He was rude to the waiter.

variants.head: impolite

example.en: It's impolite to interrupt.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，比 rude 轻；像在讲规矩。

variants.head: disrespectful

example.en: That comment was disrespectful.

variants.note_zh: 强调不尊重人，比 rude 重。

variants.head: out of line

example.en: That joke was out of line.

variants.note_zh: 口语，指言行越界；不是“排队出列”。

example.en: The neighbors are friendly.

variants.head: welcoming

example.en: The staff were very welcoming.

variants.note_zh: 偏场所/接待，让人一进来就舒服。

variants.head: approachable

example.en: The boss is approachable.

variants.note_zh: 强调敢去问、敢搭话；不是“友好”。

variants.head: warm

example.en: She has a warm personality.

variants.note_zh: 偏性格温暖，比 friendly 更感性。

example.en: He's shy around new people.

variants.head: reserved

example.en: He's reserved until you know him.

variants.note_zh: 中性，指不爱表现；不是“冷淡”。

variants.head: timid

example.en: The dog was timid around strangers.

variants.note_zh: 偏害怕、缺乏自信；比 shy 更弱。

variants.head: introverted

example.en: She's introverted but friendly.

variants.note_zh: 性格类型词，不是“害羞”；和 outgoing 相对。

example.en: She's outgoing and makes friends fast.
example.zh: 她外向，很快就交到朋友。

variants.head: sociable

example.en: He's sociable and knows everyone.

variants.note_zh: 偏爱和人打交道；比 outgoing 更强调社交。

variants.head: extroverted

example.en: She's extroverted and loves crowds.

variants.note_zh: 性格类型词，和 introverted 相对。

variants.head: a people person

example.en: She's a people person.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调擅长和人相处；比 outgoing 更具体。

example.en: It was brave of you to speak up.
example.zh: 你敢站出来说话，很勇敢。

variants.head: courageous

example.en: It was a courageous decision.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，强调面对危险仍行动；比 brave 书面。

variants.head: fearless

example.en: She's fearless on stage.

variants.note_zh: 程度重，强调不怕；比 brave 更绝对。

variants.head: gutsy

example.en: That was a gutsy move.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调敢冒险；比 brave 更随意。

example.en: She's strong after everything that happened.

variants.head: tough

example.en: She's tough; she'll get through it.

variants.note_zh: 口语，指心理/身体扛得住；不是“难”。

variants.head: resilient

example.en: Kids are resilient after setbacks.
example.zh: 孩子受挫后恢复得很快。

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，强调受挫后恢复；比 strong 更具体。

variants.head: sturdy

example.en: The table is sturdy.

variants.note_zh: 多指物体结实；说人时偏“壮实”。

example.en: He's rich but lives simply.

variants.head: wealthy

example.en: They live in a wealthy neighborhood.
example.zh: 他们住在一个富裕的小区。

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，比 rich 委婉。

variants.head: well-off

example.en: Her family is well-off.

variants.note_zh: 委婉，指经济宽裕；比 rich 轻。

variants.head: loaded

example.en: His new boss is loaded.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调非常有钱；也可指“装满了”。

example.en: Be polite even when you're upset.

variants.head: courteous

example.en: The staff were courteous.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，比 polite 书面；多用于服务场合。

variants.head: well-mannered

example.en: Their kids are well-mannered.

variants.note_zh: 强调从小养成的举止；比 polite 更具体。

variants.head: respectful

example.en: Be respectful of other people's time.

variants.note_zh: 强调尊重，比 polite 更重；常和 of 连用。

example.en: She's hardworking and never complains.

variants.head: diligent

example.en: He's a diligent student.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，强调认真持续；比 hardworking 书面。

variants.head: dedicated

example.en: She's dedicated to her team.

variants.note_zh: 强调愿意投入时间精力；比 hardworking 更带感情。

variants.head: a workaholic

example.en: He's a workaholic; he never stops.

variants.note_zh: 口语，带一点批评；不是单纯“勤奋”。

example.en: That was a stupid mistake.

variants.head: silly

example.en: It was a silly mistake.

variants.note_zh: 轻，常带亲切/自嘲；不如 stupid 伤人。

variants.head: dumb

example.en: That was a dumb idea.

variants.note_zh: 美式口语，直接但偏轻；说人时可能冒犯。

variants.head: foolish

example.en: It was a foolish choice.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，指判断不明智；比 stupid 书面。

example.en: I felt weak after the flu.

variants.head: frail

example.en: The old man is frail.

variants.note_zh: 多指老人/身体单薄；比 weak 更具体。

variants.head: feeble

example.en: His voice was feeble.

variants.note_zh: 偏书面，程度重；日常口语少用。

variants.head: shaky

example.en: My legs were shaky after the run.

variants.note_zh: 强调站不稳/发抖；比 weak 更具体。

example.en: They were poor but happy.

variants.head: broke

example.en: I'm broke until payday.

variants.note_zh: 口语，指手头暂时没钱；不是长期贫困。

variants.head: hard up

example.en: We're a bit hard up this month.
example.zh: 这个月我们手头有点紧。

variants.note_zh: 口语，偏暂时缺钱；比 poor 委婉。

variants.head: struggling

example.en: The family is struggling.

variants.note_zh: 强调经济上撑得辛苦；比 poor 更具体。

example.en: You're still young; take your time.

variants.head: youthful

example.en: She has a youthful energy.

variants.note_zh: 偏褒义，强调活力；不一定年纪小。

variants.head: little

example.en: He's still little; he can't swim alone.
example.zh: 他还小，不能一个人游泳。

variants.note_zh: 口语，多指小孩；比 young 更具体。

variants.head: junior

example.en: She's still junior in the team.

variants.note_zh: 职场里指资历浅，不是年龄小。

example.en: My grandpa is old but still active.
example.zh: 我爷爷年纪大了，但还很活跃。

variants.head: elderly

example.en: An elderly couple lives next door.
example.zh: 隔壁住着一对年长的夫妻。

variants.note_zh: 礼貌说法，比 old 委婉；多指老人。

variants.head: senior

example.en: She's a senior member of the team.
example.zh: 她是团队里的资深成员。

variants.note_zh: 职场里指资历深；也可礼貌指年长。

variants.head: up there

example.en: He's getting up there in years.

variants.note_zh: 口语委婉，常和 getting 连用；不是“在上面”。

example.en: Her apartment is stylish and simple.
example.zh: 她的公寓很有型，也很简洁。

variants.head: fashionable

example.en: That coat is very fashionable.

variants.note_zh: 强调跟潮流；比 stylish 更看流行。

variants.head: chic

example.en: The cafe has a chic look.

variants.note_zh: 偏时尚/设计，强调简洁高级；口语少用。

variants.head: trendy

example.en: It's a trendy neighborhood.

variants.note_zh: 强调当下流行；可能带一点“太追潮流”的意味。

example.en: He's handsome in a simple way.

variants.head: good-looking

example.en: Her brother is good-looking.

variants.note_zh: 最通用，男女都能用；比 handsome 随意。

variants.head: attractive

example.en: He's attractive and easy to talk to.
example.zh: 他很有吸引力，也好说话。

variants.note_zh: 偏整体魅力，不只看脸；比 handsome 宽。

variants.head: sharp-looking

example.en: He looks sharp in that suit.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调打扮利落；不是五官帅。

example.en: Their puppy is really cute.

variants.head: adorable

example.en: The baby is adorable.

variants.note_zh: 比 cute 更强调惹人喜爱；口语常用。

variants.head: charming

example.en: It's a charming little town.
example.zh: 这是个很有魅力的小镇。

variants.note_zh: 偏气质/氛围，不只是外表可爱。

variants.head: precious

example.en: Look at those precious little hands.

variants.note_zh: 多用于婴儿/小动物，带疼爱；不是“珍贵”时的正式用法。

example.en: This app is useful for learning words.
example.zh: 这个 App 背单词很有用。

variants.head: handy

example.en: A small umbrella is handy in this city.
example.zh: 在这座城市，小伞很好用。

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调方便顺手；比 useful 更随意。

variants.head: practical

example.en: It's a practical gift.

variants.note_zh: 强调能解决实际问题；比 useful 更具体。

variants.head: helpful

example.en: The staff were very helpful.

variants.note_zh: 多指人或建议有帮助；比 useful 更常修饰人。

example.en: It's important to read the contract.

variants.head: crucial

example.en: Sleep is crucial before an exam.

variants.note_zh: 比 important 重，强调决定成败。

variants.head: essential

example.en: Water is essential for life.

variants.note_zh: 强调缺了不行；比 important 更绝对。

variants.head: key

example.en: The key thing is to stay calm.

variants.note_zh: 口语，常作定语；比 important 更简短有力。

example.en: That road is dangerous at night.

variants.head: risky

example.en: It's risky to drive in the fog.

variants.note_zh: 强调可能出问题；不一定是人身危险。

variants.head: unsafe

example.en: The building is unsafe.

variants.note_zh: 偏客观判断；比 dangerous 正式。

variants.head: hazardous

example.en: Hazardous waste needs special handling.

variants.note_zh: 正式/书面，多指化学品、环境危害。

example.en: The neighborhood is safe at night.

variants.head: secure

example.en: The building is secure.

variants.note_zh: 强调有防护、不易出事；比 safe 正式。

variants.head: out of danger

example.en: The patient is out of danger.

variants.note_zh: 多用于病人/事故后；不是“安全的地方”。

variants.head: in good hands

example.en: The kids are in good hands.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调有人负责；不是字面“在好手里”。

example.en: My desk is messy after a deadline.
example.zh: 赶完截止日期我的桌子很乱。

variants.head: cluttered

example.en: The room is cluttered with boxes.
example.zh: 房间里堆满箱子，很杂乱。

variants.note_zh: 强调东西多、堆着；比 messy 更具体。

variants.head: untidy

example.en: His desk is always untidy.

variants.note_zh: 偏英式/正式；美式更常说 messy。

variants.head: a mess

example.en: The kitchen is a mess.

variants.note_zh: 口语最常用，程度比 messy 重。

example.en: Her desk is always neat.

variants.head: tidy

example.en: Keep your room tidy.

variants.note_zh: 和 neat 基本同义，偏英式常用；美式也用。

variants.head: organized

example.en: She is very organized at work.

variants.note_zh: 强调安排有序；不只看桌面。

variants.head: spotless

example.en: The kitchen was spotless.

variants.note_zh: 强调干净到没有污点；比 neat 更重。

example.en: The subway is crowded at eight.

variants.head: packed

example.en: The mall is packed on weekends.

variants.note_zh: 口语，比 crowded 更强调满。

variants.head: jammed

example.en: The road was jammed.

variants.note_zh: 口语，可指人挤或车堵；比 crowded 更随意。

variants.head: shoulder to shoulder

example.en: We stood shoulder to shoulder on the bus.

variants.note_zh: 形象说法，强调人多到贴着；比 crowded 更具体。

example.en: I'm ready when you are.

variants.head: set

example.en: We're all set to go.

variants.note_zh: 口语，常和 all 连用；比 ready 更强调“就绪”。

variants.head: all set

example.en: I'm all set; let's go.

variants.note_zh: 口语固定说法，比 ready 更完整。

variants.head: good to go

example.en: The car is good to go.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调可以开始/出发；比 ready 更随意。

example.en: I'm late; the meeting started.
example.zh: 我迟到了，会已经开始了。

variants.head: behind schedule

example.en: The train is behind schedule.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，指比计划晚；多用于交通/项目。

variants.head: running behind

example.en: We're running behind by ten minutes.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调进度落后；常和 by 连用。

variants.head: overdue

example.en: The library book is overdue.

variants.note_zh: 强调超过期限；不是“迟到的人”。

example.en: I'm early, so I'll wait outside.

variants.head: ahead of schedule

example.en: The project finished ahead of schedule.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，指比计划早；多用于项目/工程。

variants.head: ahead of time

example.en: She arrived ahead of time.

variants.note_zh: 比 early 更强调“提前完成/到达”。

variants.head: in advance

example.en: Book the tickets in advance.

variants.note_zh: 强调事先做；不一定是“早到”。

example.en: The museum is free on Mondays.

variants.head: complimentary

example.en: The hotel offers a complimentary breakfast.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式/酒店服务；比 free 更礼貌。

variants.head: on the house

example.en: The dessert is on the house.

variants.note_zh: 口语，指店家免费送；不是“在房子上”。

variants.head: no charge

example.en: There's no charge for delivery.

variants.note_zh: 偏服务/账单，强调不收费；比 free 具体。

example.en: The room is available after three.

variants.head: free

example.en: Are you free on Friday?

variants.note_zh: 口语，最常用；也说房间/座位空着。

variants.head: open

example.en: The slot is still open.

variants.note_zh: 偏日程/名额，强调还没被占。

variants.head: up for grabs

example.en: The last ticket is up for grabs.
example.zh: 最后一张票谁抢到算谁的。

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调先到先得；比 available 更随意。

example.en: That building is ugly.

variants.head: unattractive

example.en: The design is unattractive.

variants.note_zh: 礼貌说法，比 ugly 委婉；说人时也更安全。

variants.head: hideous

example.en: That wallpaper is hideous.

variants.note_zh: 程度重，口语；比 ugly 更夸张。

variants.head: not much to look at

example.en: The hotel is not much to look at.

variants.note_zh: 口语委婉，强调外观普通；不是“没什么可看”。

example.en: He's tall enough to reach the shelf.

variants.head: lanky

example.en: He's a lanky teenager.

variants.note_zh: 偏瘦长、手脚长；比 tall 更具体。

variants.head: towering

example.en: The building is towering.

variants.note_zh: 偏书面，多指建筑/身材高大。

variants.head: high

example.en: The ceiling is very high.

variants.note_zh: 用于物体高度；说人高用 tall，不用 high。

example.en: I'm short, so I need a stool.

variants.head: petite

example.en: She's petite and buys small sizes.

variants.note_zh: 礼貌说法，多用于女性/服装；比 short 委婉。

variants.head: small

example.en: He's small for his age.

variants.note_zh: 中性，指体型小；比 short 更宽。

variants.head: on the short side

example.en: The door is on the short side.

variants.note_zh: 口语委婉，强调略低于平均；也可说人。

example.en: The box is big but light.

variants.head: huge

example.en: The new mall is huge.

variants.note_zh: 口语最常用，比 big 重。

variants.head: massive

example.en: There was a massive crowd.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式/书面，强调体量；比 huge 稍正式。

variants.head: enormous

example.en: The project is enormous.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，强调超出常规；可指规模。

example.en: The apartment is small but cozy.

variants.head: tiny

example.en: The kitchen is tiny.

variants.note_zh: 口语，比 small 更强调小。

variants.head: little

example.en: They live in a little house.
example.zh: 他们住在一间小房子里。

variants.note_zh: 口语，常带亲切感；比 small 更主观。

variants.head: compact

example.en: The car is compact and easy to park.

variants.note_zh: 褒义，强调小而实用；不是单纯“小”。

example.en: The box is too heavy to carry alone.
example.zh: 箱子太重，一个人搬不动。

variants.head: weighty

example.en: It's a weighty package.

variants.note_zh: 偏书面，强调分量；也可比喻话题沉重。

variants.head: hefty

example.en: That's a hefty bag.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调又大又重；常指价格/账单。

variants.head: on the heavy side

example.en: The laptop is on the heavy side.

variants.note_zh: 口语委婉，强调比预期重。

example.en: The bag is light enough to carry all day.

variants.head: lightweight

example.en: It's a lightweight jacket.

variants.note_zh: 中性描述，强调重量轻；比 light 具体。

variants.head: feather-light

example.en: The new phone is feather-light.

variants.note_zh: 夸张说法，强调非常轻。

variants.head: easy to carry

example.en: The stroller is easy to carry.

variants.note_zh: 口语，从使用角度说轻便；不是单纯重量。

example.en: The cat is fat and lazy.

variants.head: overweight

example.en: The doctor said he's overweight.

variants.note_zh: 礼貌/医学说法，比 fat 委婉。

variants.head: heavy

example.en: He's a heavy man.

variants.note_zh: 委婉，强调体重；比 fat 客气。

variants.head: big

example.en: He's big but fast.

variants.note_zh: 口语委婉，常指块头大；不一定是胖。

example.en: He's thin but strong.

variants.head: slim

example.en: She stays slim by walking.

variants.note_zh: 褒义，强调身材好；比 thin 正面。

variants.head: skinny

example.en: He's skinny but eats a lot.

variants.note_zh: 口语，强调瘦得明显；说人时可能不太礼貌。

variants.head: slender

example.en: She has slender hands.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式/褒义，强调线条细；比 thin 优雅。
